questions.q: What is mongosh, and what did it replace?
options: MongoDB's current, actively-developed command-line shell, which replaced the legacy `mongo` shell
A cloud-only shell with no local connection support
A GUI tool that replaced MongoDB Compass
A deprecated tool being replaced by the legacy `mongo` shell
questions.explain: mongosh is the current shell; the legacy `mongo` shell is deprecated and no longer bundled as the default starting with MongoDB 6.0.

questions.q: What happens if you call `db.users.insertOne({...})` on a collection that doesn't exist yet?
options: The command fails with an error requiring you to create the collection first
It inserts into a default fallback collection instead
MongoDB creates the collection automatically on the first insert
MongoDB silently discards the insert
questions.explain: Consistent with MongoDB's schema-less-by-default model, collections are created automatically on first write.

options: Only the first matching document
A cursor over every document in the users collection where loyaltyTier equals "gold"
A count of matching documents
Every document in the collection, ignoring the filter
questions.explain: find() takes a filter document and returns a cursor over all matches; findOne() is the one that returns just the first match.

questions.q: What does the `$set` operator do in an update command like `updateOne({filter}, { $set: { loyaltyTier: "platinum" } })`?
options: Updates only the named field(s), leaving the rest of the document untouched
Deletes every field not explicitly listed
Creates a new document instead of updating the existing one
Replaces the entire document with only the listed fields
questions.explain: $set is scoped to the fields you name — it does not touch or remove any other field in the document.

questions.q: Why is `db.users.deleteMany({})` considered genuinely destructive, per this lesson?
options: It deletes the entire database, not just the collection
deleteMany requires a non-empty filter and would simply error out
An empty filter matches every document in the collection, so it removes all of them
It only works on empty collections, so it's harmless
questions.explain: The filter document decides what's affected — an empty filter matches everything, so deleteMany({}) clears the whole collection.
